proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(\omega(r)=\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(r)\). By the unit-radius admissibility lemma, \(1\in\mathcal R_+\), \(s_1\le\omega(1)\), and \(b_1\le\omega(1)/2\). The exact-bias conclusion of the total-modulus rule and the exact Gaussian score law give, for every \(x\in\mathcal M_{T,m}\),
\[
\mathbb E_x\!\left[\{\widehat\theta_1-\ell(x)\}^2\right]
=\operatorname{Bias}_x(\widehat\theta_1)^2+operatorname{Var}_x(\widehat\theta_1)
\le b_1^2+s_1^2
\le\frac54\omega(1)^2. \tag{7}
\]
The defining inequality for \(r_{\mathrm{MSE},j}\) implies
\[
\sup_x\mathbb E_x\!\left[
\{\widehat\theta_{r_{\mathrm{MSE},j}}-\ell(x)\}^2\right]
\le(1+j^{-1})\inf_{r\in\mathcal R_+}(b_r^2+s_r^2).
\]
Taking \(j\to\infty\), and using \(r=1\) as an admissible competitor in the infimum, proves the last inequality in the theorem. Since \(R^\star\) is the infimum over all measurable estimators, it is no larger than the worst-case risk of each displayed estimator, which proves the middle inequality.

For the converse, let \(x^-_1,x^+_1\) be the canonical modulus endpoints at radius one, set \(P_-=\mathcal N(Kx^-_1,\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}})\), \(P_+=\mathcal N(Kx^+_1,\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}})\), and put \(\Delta=\ell(x^+_1)-\ell(x^-_1)=\omega(1)\). With \(d=K(x^+_1-x^-_1)\), the constraint gives \(d'\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}^{-1}d\le1\). Direct integration of the equal-covariance Gaussian likelihood ratio gives
\[
\chi^2(P_+,P_-)
=\mathbb E_{P_-}\left[\left(\frac{dP_+}{dP_-}-1\right)^2\right]
=\exp\!\left(d'\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}^{-1}d\right)-1
\le e-1.
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz applied to the likelihood ratio yields
\[
\operatorname{TV}(P_+,P_-)
=\frac12\mathbb E_{P_-}\left|\frac{dP_+}{dP_-}-1\right|
\le\frac12\sqrt{e-1}. \tag{8}
\]
For an arbitrary measurable estimator \(\widetilde\theta\), let \(A\) be the event that \(\widetilde\theta\) is at least the midpoint of \(\ell(x^-_1)\) and \(\ell(x^+_1)\). On \(A\) under \(P_-\), and on \(A^c\) under \(P_+\), squared error is at least \(\Delta^2/4\). Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sup_{x\in\mathcal M_{T,m}}
\mathbb E_x[(\widetilde\theta-\ell(x))^2]
&\ge\frac12\left\{
\mathbb E_{P_-}(\widetilde\theta-\ell(x^-_1))^2+
\mathbb E_{P_+}(\widetilde\theta-\ell(x^+_1))^2\right\}\\
&\ge\frac{\Delta^2}{8}\{P_-(A)+P_+(A^c)\}\\
&\ge\frac{\Delta^2}{8}\{1-\operatorname{TV}(P_+,P_-)\}\\
&\ge\frac{1-\frac12\sqrt{e-1}}8\,\omega(1)^2,
\end{aligned}
\]
where the penultimate line is the definition of total variation and the last uses (8). Taking the infimum over \(\widetilde\theta\) proves the lower bound.

Fix \(j\), and abbreviate \(r=r_{\mathrm{CI},j}\), \(b=b_r\), and \(s=s_r>0\). The exact Gaussian score law and the exact-bias part of the total-modulus rule imply that, for every \(x\in\mathcal M_{T,m}\),
\[
\frac{\widehat\theta_r-\ell(x)}s\sim\mathcal N(t_x,1),
\qquad |t_x|\le b/s. \tag{9}
\]
For fixed \(c\ge0\), the function
\[
p_c(t)=\Pr\{|\mathcal N(t,1)|\le c\}=\Phi(c-t)-\Phi(-c-t)
\]
is even. For \(t\ge0\), differentiation gives \(p_c'(t)=-\phi(c-t)+\phi(c+t)\le0\), because \(|c-t|\le c+t\) and the standard-normal density decreases with absolute value. Thus (9) and the definition of \(\operatorname{cv}_\alpha\) give
\[
\Pr_x\{\ell(x)\in C_{\alpha,j}(Z)\}
=p_{\operatorname{cv}_\alpha(b/s)}(t_x)
\ge p_{\operatorname{cv}_\alpha(b/s)}(b/s)
\ge1-\alpha.
\]
The deterministic half-length is \(s_r\operatorname{cv}_\alpha(b_r/s_r)\). Its claimed factor \(1+j^{-1}\) optimality is exactly the defining inequality for \(r_{\mathrm{CI},j}\).

For the upper expected-length bound, the unit-radius admissibility lemma permits \(r=1\) as a competitor. The event \(|\mathcal N(0,1)|\le z_\alpha\) has probability \(1-\alpha\), and the triangle inequality shows
\[
\{|\mathcal N(0,1)|\le z_\alpha\}
\subseteq
\{|\mathcal N(t,1)|\le t+z_\alpha\}
\qquad(t\ge0).
\]
Hence \(\operatorname{cv}_\alpha(t)\le t+z_\alpha\). With \(b_1\le\omega(1)/2\) and \(s_1\le\omega(1)\), where again \(\omega=\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}\),
\[
2s_1\operatorname{cv}_\alpha(b_1/s_1)
\le2b_1+2z_\alpha s_1
\le(1+2z_\alpha)\omega(1). \tag{10}
\]
The infimum-approaching property of \(r_{\mathrm{CI},j}\), followed by \(j\to\infty\), proves the final upper bound. Every \(C_{\alpha,j}\) is admissible for the definition of \(\operatorname{EL}_\alpha^\star\), so the middle inequality follows.

It remains to prove the lower bound for an arbitrary measurable interval procedure \(C\) with uniform coverage at least \(1-\alpha\). Since \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\),
\[
0<r_\alpha=\sqrt{\log\{1+(1-2\alpha)^2\}}<1.
\]
Let \(x^-_{r_\alpha},x^+_{r_\alpha}\) be the canonical modulus endpoints, let \(P_-\) and \(P_+\) be their score laws, and set \(\Delta=\omega(r_\alpha)\). The same direct Gaussian likelihood-ratio and Cauchy--Schwarz calculation as in the minimax proof gives
\[
\operatorname{TV}(P_+,P_-)
\le\frac12\sqrt{\exp(r_\alpha^2)-1}
=\frac{1-2\alpha}{2}. \tag{11}
\]
Write \(A_-\) and \(A_+\) for the events that \(C(Z)\) contains \(\ell(x^-_{r_\alpha})\) and \(\ell(x^+_{r_\alpha})\), respectively. Honesty and total variation imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_-(A_-\cap A_+)
&\ge1-P_-(A_-^c)-P_-(A_+^c)\\
&\ge1-\alpha-\{P_+(A_+^c)+\operatorname{TV}(P_+,P_-)\}\\
&\ge1-2\alpha-\operatorname{TV}(P_+,P_-)\\
&\ge\frac{1-2\alpha}{2}. \tag{12}
\end{aligned}
\]
Because \(C(Z)\) is an interval, its length is at least \(\Delta\) on \(A_-\cap A_+\). Equations (11)--(12) yield
\[
\sup_x\mathbb E_x[\operatorname{length}C(Z)]
\ge\mathbb E_{P_-}[\operatorname{length}C(Z)]
\ge\frac{1-2\alpha}{2}\omega(r_\alpha). \tag{13}
\]
Concavity of the nonnegative modulus gives
\[
\omega(r_\alpha)\ge r_\alpha\omega(1)+(1-r_\alpha)\omega(0)
\ge r_\alpha\omega(1).
\]
Substitution into (13), followed by the infimum over all honest measurable interval-valued \(C\), proves \(\operatorname{EL}_\alpha^\star\ge c_\alpha\omega(1)\). The argument used only the exact nested modulus, so it makes no calendar-rate claim.

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \(\beta\in(0,1]\) and finite constants \(C_H,C_D>0\). Set \(q_j=1/T\), \(m=1\), and \(k=\lfloor T^{3/4}\rfloor\). For an array \(a=(a_{g,t}:1\le g\le t\le T-1)\), define
\[
A_t=\sum_{g=1}^t a_{g,t},\qquad v_{j,t}=a_{j,t}\mathbf 1\{j\le t\},\qquad d_j=(b^{\prime}a)_j=\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}\sum_{g=1}^t b_{(g,t),j}a_{g,t}.
\]
If
\[
\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}A_t=1,\qquad
\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}|A_t|\left(\frac{T-t}{T}\right)^\beta\le C_H\left(\frac{k}{T}\right)^\beta,\qquad
\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}\inf_{c\in\mathbb R}\|v_t-cq\|_1\le C_D\frac{k}{T-k},
\]
then there is \(T_0=T_0(\beta,C_H,C_D)\) such that, for every \(T\ge T_0\),
\[
\sum_{j=1}^T\frac{d_j^2}{q_j}\ge\frac1{16}.
\]
Consequently, for no fixed \(C_E<\infty\) can arrays satisfying the three displays also satisfy \(\sum_jd_j^2/q_j\le C_ET/k^2\) for all sufficiently large \(T\). Thus the proposed certificate consisting of separate normalization, Holder-leverage, bounded-deviation-leverage, and \(O(T/k^2)\) shared-baseline-energy inequalities is impossible uniformly. This conclusion does not rule out every bounded lift and does not assert either equivalence or nonequivalence between \(\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(1)\) and the candidate diagnostic \(\rho_{N,T,m}\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Choose a fixed \(\lambda>0\) such that
\[
\eta:=C_H\lambda^{-\beta}<\frac18.
\]
For each \(t\), the continuous coercive function \(c\mapsto\|v_t-cq\|_1\) has a minimizer; fix one, call it \(c_t\), and write
\[
\varepsilon_t=v_t-c_tq,\qquad e_t=\|\varepsilon_t\|_1,\qquad D_T=\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}e_t.
\]
The third displayed hypothesis gives
\[
D_T\le C_D\frac{k}{T-k}=o(1),
\]
because \(k=\lfloor T^{3/4}\rfloor\). Since \(\sum_jq_j=1\) and \(\sum_jv_{j,t}=A_t\),
\[
|A_t-c_t|=\left|\sum_{j=1}^T\varepsilon_{j,t}\right|\le e_t. \tag{1}
\]

Let
\[
J=\{t\in\{1,\ldots,T-1\}:T-t\le\lambda k\},
\qquad
E=\{j\in\{1,\ldots,T\}:j\le T-\lambda k\}.
\]
Integer inequalities are understood literally, so \(q(E)=|E|/T\ge1-\lambda k/T-1/T=1-o(1)\). If \(t\notin J\), then \(((T-t)/T)^\beta>(\lambda k/T)^\beta\). The Holder-leverage hypothesis therefore implies
\[
\sum_{t\notin J}|A_t|
\le \left(\frac{T}{\lambda k}\right)^\beta
\sum_{t\notin J}|A_t|\left(\frac{T-t}{T}\right)^\beta
\le C_H\lambda^{-\beta}=\eta. \tag{2}
\]
Using the normalization, (1), and (2),
\[
\sum_{t\in J}c_t
\ge \sum_{t\in J}A_t-\sum_{t\in J}e_t
=1-\sum_{t\notin J}A_t-\sum_{t\in J}e_t
\ge1-\eta-D_T. \tag{3}
\]

The baseline-loading definition and \(q_{>t}=\sum_{j>t}q_j\) give
\[
\sum_{j\in E}d_j
=\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}H_t,
\qquad
H_t=-\sum_{j\in E}v_{j,t}
+A_t\frac{q(E\cap C_t)}{q_{>t}}. \tag{4}
\]
For \(t\in J\), every \(j\in E\) satisfies \(j\le t\), hence \(E\cap C_t=\varnothing\). Thus, by (3),
\[
\left|\sum_{t\in J}H_t\right|
=\left|-q(E)\sum_{t\in J}c_t-
\sum_{t\in J}\sum_{j\in E}\varepsilon_{j,t}\right|
\ge q(E)(1-\eta-D_T)-D_T. \tag{5}
\]
For \(t\notin J\), put \(p_t=q(E\cap C_t)/q_{>t}\in[0,1]\). Since \(A_t=c_t+\sum_j\varepsilon_{j,t}\), equation (4) becomes
\[
H_t=c_t\{p_t-q(E)\}
+p_t\sum_j\varepsilon_{j,t}-\sum_{j\in E}\varepsilon_{j,t}.
\]
Equation (1) yields \(|c_t|\le|A_t|+e_t\), and hence
\[
|H_t|\le |A_t|+3e_t.
\]
Together with (2), this implies
\[
\left|\sum_{t\notin J}H_t\right|\le\eta+3D_T. \tag{6}
\]
Combining (4)--(6),
\[
\left|\sum_{j\in E}d_j\right|
\ge q(E)(1-\eta-D_T)-\eta-4D_T.
\]
The right-hand side converges to \(1-2\eta>3/4\). Enlarging \(T_0\), if necessary, therefore makes it at least \(1/4\). Weighted Cauchy--Schwarz now gives
\[
\sum_{j=1}^T\frac{d_j^2}{q_j}
\ge\sum_{j\in E}\frac{d_j^2}{q_j}
\ge\frac{\left(\sum_{j\in E}d_j\right)^2}{\sum_{j\in E}q_j}
\ge\frac1{16},
\]
because \(\sum_{j\in E}q_j\le1\). Finally, \(T/k^2\to0\), so the lower bound \(1/16\) contradicts \(\sum_jd_j^2/q_j\le C_ET/k^2\) for any fixed \(C_E\) and all sufficiently large \(T\). This proves precisely the asserted certificate obstruction.

added_lemmas.statement:
In the nested Gaussian experiment, every \(r>0\) belongs to \(\mathcal R_+\). More precisely, if \(e=(\mathbf 1_T,0)\), then every canonical maximizer exhausts the constraint \(\|Kh_r\|_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}^{-1}}=r\), and
\[
\omega'_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(r)\ge
\|Ke\|_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}^{-1}}^{-1}>0,
\qquad
0<s_r=\omega'_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(r)
\le\frac{\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(r)-\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(0)}{r}
\le\frac{\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(r)}r.
\]
In particular, \(1\in\mathcal R_+\), \(0<s_1\le\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(1)\), and \(0\le b_1\le\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(1)/2\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The score index set is nonempty because \(T\ge3\), \(m\le\delta T\), and \(\delta<1\). Since \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}\) is positive definite, \(D:=\|Ke\|_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}^{-1}}=\|\mathbf1_O\|_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}^{-1}}>0\). Adding an arbitrary multiple of \(e\) changes every coordinate of the calendar path by the same constant and leaves the cohort deviations unchanged. It therefore preserves the Holder restriction, the deviation bound, and calendar centering. Hence \(e\) is a two-sided recession direction of the difference class \(2\mathcal M_{T,m}(\beta,L,B,q)\), with \(\ell(e)=1\).

If a maximizer \(h_r\) had \(\|Kh_r\|_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}^{-1}}<r\), then \(h_r+ce\) would remain feasible for all sufficiently small \(c>0\), by the triangle inequality, while \(\ell(h_r+ce)=\ell(h_r)+c\); this contradicts maximality. Thus the constraint is active. Similarly, for \(r_2>r_1>0\), the vector
\[
h_{r_1}+\frac{r_2-r_1}{D}e
\]
belongs to the difference class and is feasible at radius \(r_2\). Consequently
\[
\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(r_2)-
\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(r_1)
\ge\frac{r_2-r_1}{D}.
\]
Taking the right derivative and using the established concavity and supergradient property of the modulus yields \(\omega'_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(r)\ge D^{-1}>0\). Thus \(r\in\mathcal R_+\). The supergradient inequality at \(r\), evaluated at zero, is
\[
\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(0)
\le\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(r)-r\omega'_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(r),
\]
which proves the two upper bounds on \(s_r\). The definitions of \(s_1\) and \(b_1=\{\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(1)-s_1\}/2\) give the final assertions.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Uniformly over \(N/T\ge1\) and \(1\le m\le\delta T\), let
\[
c_R=\frac{1-\frac12\sqrt{e-1}}8.
\]
Then the exact nested-covariance modulus satisfies
\[
c_R\,\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(1)^2
\le R^{\star}
\le\liminf_{j\to\infty}\sup_{x\in\mathcal M_{T,m}}
\mathbb E_x\!\left[

\right]

\]
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The exact Gaussian modulus comparison is proved with the mandated constants, whereas no comparison between the nested modulus and the candidate calendar diagnostic has been proved. The former phase-envelope and nested homogeneous-rate clauses were therefore too strong.

For every \(j\in\mathbb N\), \(C_{\alpha,j}(Z)\) is a measurable interval and satisfies
\[
\inf_{x\in\mathcal M_{T,m}}\Pr_x\{\ell(x)\in C_{\alpha,j}(Z)\}\ge1-\alpha.
\]
Its half-length is within the factor \(1+j^{-1}\) of the infimum over the positive-standard-deviation affine modulus intervals. Define
\[
r_\alpha=\sqrt{\log\{1+(1-2\alpha)^2\}},
\qquad

The lower bound is over measurable interval-valued procedures.

prose_updates.tldr: A fixed-cohort repeated-cross-section event study induces an exact Gaussian not-yet-treated score experiment with shrinking control pools and nested shared-baseline covariance. The contribution is now stated at the operator-specific frontier that is proved: global minimax MSE is bounded above and below by explicit constants times \(\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(1)^2\), and measurable uniformly honest intervals have expected length bounded by explicit constants times \(\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(1)\). A new equal-share obstruction theorem shows that the proposed separate Holder-leverage, cohort-deviation-leverage, and \(O(T/k^2)\) baseline-energy certificate cannot hold at \(m=1\), \(k=\lfloor T^{3/4}\rfloor\). The matched-date-block calculation remains an exact marginal diagnostic for \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{diag}}\) only. Converting the exact nested modulus to a closed-form calendar rate remains open.

project_justification.gap: Staggered-DiD methods diagnose the loss of valid late comparisons, while Gaussian optimal-recovery theory starts from a supplied operator and covariance. Neither literature derives the nested shared-baseline covariance of these not-yet-treated scores or determines how that covariance obstructs a natural calendar-rate certificate.
project_justification.niche: The causal design creates a finite but growing Gaussian inverse problem in which the same baseline cells couple all comparison dates. This operator admits exact modulus-based risk and honest-length analysis, yet its baseline Gram term prevents a tempting datewise information argument.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the nested covariance, proves an equal-share baseline-energy obstruction for the proposed four-part dual certificate, constructs total measurable modulus estimators and bias-aware intervals, and matches their global MSE and honest expected length to the exact nested modulus with explicit constants. The closed-form calendar conversion is isolated as an open problem rather than claimed.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance function is estimated inside the exact known-covariance Gaussian score experiment. Holder calendar paths and bounded centered cohort deviations define the law class; no bounded-lift or calendar-rate equivalence is imposed as an assumption.

prose_updates.related_work: Callaway and Sant'Anna supply the group-time effects and calendar aggregation that give the target its causal interpretation. Borusyak, Jaravel, and Spiess show in Section 3.3, Proposition 5, why long-run event-study effects lose valid comparisons, motivating explicit extrapolation. Sant'Anna and Zhao give a two-period repeated-cross-section efficiency benchmark, whereas the covariance lemma here derives the growing-calendar nested score law. Donoho's 1994 model (equation (1)), Theorem 1, and Section 11 provide Gaussian modulus machinery conditional on a supplied operator. Armstrong and Kolesar's 2018 Section 3.2, equations (23)--(26), and their 2020 equation (15) and Theorem 3.1 on pp. 15--16 provide bias-aware Gaussian interval and Holder-regression calibrations conditional on supplied weights. None supplies a bounded right inverse for the staggered-DiD baseline Gram term. The new contribution is therefore the design-derived nested covariance, the operator-specific baseline-energy obstruction, and the exact-modulus consequences; the matched-date-block calculation is supporting calibration only and does not transfer its rate to \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}\). Rambachan and Roth concern sensitivity to trend violations rather than bounded treatment-effect heterogeneity, and Cohen and Fogarty motivate covariance-order diagnostics without implying an ordering here.
prose_updates.interpretation: The exact modulus \(\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(1)\) is computable from the finite-dimensional convex program defined by the observed score operator, the known nested covariance, and the Holder-plus-bounded-cohort class. It is the proved difficulty scale for both point estimation and honest intervals. The candidate \(\rho_{N,T,m}\) remains useful for diagnosing three intuitive calendar components, but its minimizer \(k^\star\) is not established as an oracle depth for the nested experiment. The obstruction identifies the shared baseline, rather than contemporaneous date-block noise, as the precise failure of the proposed separate dual bounds.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The obstruction theorem rules out the proposed four-separate-inequality dual certificate uniformly at equal shares, \(m=1\), and \(k=\lfloor T^{3/4}\rfloor\); it does not prove that every bounded lift is impossible and does not prove that the exact nested modulus is or is not comparable to the candidate calendar diagnostic. The matched comparison deletes only cross-date dependence while preserving each full within-date covariance block, so its finite information sum and homogeneous Holder rate apply only to \(\Sigma_{\mathrm{diag}}\). Equal block marginals do not order the nested and block-diagonal experiments. Non-Gaussian coupling and nuisance estimation remain outside the exact score experiment.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved headline consists of the exact nested score covariance, the equal-share baseline-covariance certificate obstruction, explicit-constant global minimax MSE bounds in terms of \(\omega_{\Sigma_{\mathrm{nest}}}(1)\), and exact-coverage bias-aware intervals whose shortest honest expected length is bounded by explicit constants times the same modulus. The interval lower bound ranges over measurable interval-valued procedures. No phase diagram or closed-form nested calendar rate is claimed. The diagnostic \(\rho_{N,T,m}\), its minimizing depth, smoothness adaptation, and any equivalence between that diagnostic and the exact modulus remain open. Generic Gaussian modulus theory and the matched-date-block calculation are supporting ingredients rather than novelty claims.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem isolates a design-specific obstruction created by reusing the same baseline cohort cells across all not-yet-treated contrasts.
statement_notes.gap: Published Gaussian modulus results condition on an operator and weights; they do not show that the natural staggered-DiD dual localization requirements force nonvanishing baseline Gram energy.
